old_title: Iran war live: Tehran mocks Trump over fake AI video of US strikes
new_title: Iran war live: Trump aides 'urgently trying to stop war escalating' despite strikes
old_text:
Iran has rubbished Donald Trump's threats against one of its key islands after the US president threatened to hit the Islamic Republic "hard" following Iranian missile strikes on US military bases.
Hamid Bovard, the chief executive of the National Iranian Oil Company, said operations on Kharg Island, a vital trade hub holding some 90 per cent of Iranian oil exports, had not stopped, after Trump posted an AI video on social media claiming it was "being blown to smithereens".
"Trump's tweets are laughable and conditions in Kharg are calm and appropriate," he said in response to the Truth Social post.
A US official also told Reuters that the US did not target Kharg Island in overnight strikes.
The latest escalation in tensions came as both sides exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with Iran attacking US bases in Jordan and the UAE in response to US attacks on Larak island.
Offering Washington a route to climb down, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would immediately reciprocate if the US honours its commitments under an interim deal signed in June to pave the way for peace talks.
The latest: Iran's president says Tehran will reciprocate if US honours interim deal commitments
Iran will immediately reciprocate if the United States returns to its commitments under an interim deal signed in June, president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday.
He made his comments at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek after the first exchange of direct attacks in the US-Iran conflict since late July, with the US striking Larak Island and Iran then launching attacks on two US air bases in Jordan.
"I am stating clearly that if the US returns to its commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate," Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by state media.
He was referring to an interim deal signed in June between Tehran and Washington in efforts to end the war, which started with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. The deal quickly unravelled amid disagreements over its implementation.
Pezeshkian said in Bishkek on Monday that war was in no one's interest and that Tehran was still open to a negotiated solution in its conflict with Washington.
Iran's Achilles Heel: Why Trump has his sights on the tiny oil hub Kharg Island
Six months into the war with Iran, US president Donald Trump has posted a fake AI video to social media, claiming that a key Iranian island was being destroyed.
The claim that Kharg Island was "blow to smithereens", accompanied by a clip of refineries exploding into flames on Truth Social, was quickly debunked by his own officials.
The US has struck Kharg before, however, with Vice President JD Vance confirming in April "military targets" on the outlet had been hit.
Here's why Kharg Island matters to Iran's economy and, by extension, to the United States military:
Vance says US now focused on free flow of commerce in Strait of Hormuz
US vice president JD Vance said Washington's immediate priority was restoring the "free flow of commerce" through the Strait of Hormuz.
He said the US strike on Larak Island was aimed at preventing Iran from laying mines in the key shipping route.
He accused Iran's leadership of acting "not with a whole lot of strategic wisdom" in trying to choke off oil and gas exports.
"What's odd to me is that they will sometimes fire at their own allies just to prevent the free flow of oil and gas," he said, calling Iran's leaders "really crazy".
Iran president tells Pakistan PM war not in Tehran's interest
Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian has told Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif that continuing the war was not in Iran's interest and said Tehran remained willing to implement a US-Iran memorandum of understanding mediated by Pakistan in June.
He spoke with Sharif on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan on Monday.
Meanwhile, Iranian state TV said the escalation between the US and Tehran followed a tanker hitting two Iranian naval mines while trying to pass through the southern Strait of Hormuz.
It said three ships had been targeted for using an unauthorised route.
The IRGC warned other vessels that they must comply with Iran's rules for passage or face the same fate.
US treasury secretary warns sanctions could trigger economic collapse in Iran within months
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said Washington's sanctions campaign is putting severe pressure on Iran's economy and could trigger an economic collapse within months unless Tehran agrees to negotiations.
Bessent said: "I would think that they are lashing out kinetically because they are losing economically."
He added that "within weeks or months" the Iranian economy could collapse, though he stressed that this "does not have to happen", saying: "We just have to have the regime come to their senses."
Bessent also warned that the US plans to impose new sanctions every week, targeting banks and potentially cutting institutions off from the dollar-based financial system.
"You're going to see a lot more of these every week," he said.
Iran calls Trump's AI video of attack on key oil export hub 'laughable'
Iran has denied Donald Trump's claim that Kharg Island, a key Iranian oil export hub, was being "blown to smithereens", calling his posts "laughable".
"Trump's tweets are laughable and conditions in Kharg are calm and appropriate," National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard was cited as saying by Nournews.
Trump had shared an AI video of the attack on Kharg Island earlier on his Truth Social.
Bovard said the island remained calm and oil operations had continued without interruption despite repeated US and Israeli attacks.
Kharg handles about 90 per cent of Iran's oil exports.
Oil prices rise amid renewed clashes between US and Iran
Oil prices rose on Tuesday as renewed fighting between the US and Iran heightened fears of disruptions to crude supplies from the oil-rich Middle East.
Brent crude futures gained 56 cents, or 0.6 per cent, to $91.05 a barrel by 0044 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 83 cents, or 1 per cent, to $86.59 a barrel.
Vance says US military is 'big enough' to handle threats, despite reports of munitions shortages
JD Vance has said the US military is "big enough" to handle threats, despite reports of munitions shortages.
"Are you concerned about reports of weapon shortages, the strain on the forces? Is the U.S. Military big enough to handle threats around the world, including China?" Fox News' Lucas Tomlinson asked the US vice president in a new interview.
"Look, we're clearly big enough to handle threats around the world, including China", Vance replied. "As the president has said, we want to have a positive relationship with the PRC [People's Republic of China]".
Hegseth hired conservative influencers who amplify his 'warrior ethos' mantra: report
A handful of high-profile conservative influencers have reportedly been working as undisclosed government employees and using their huge social media followings to praise US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and defend the Trump administration's policies.
Among them are Rob Maness, a retired Army Air Force colonel with more than 130,000 followers on X, and Kurt Schlichter, a retired Army colonel with more than 600,000 followers on X, according to the Washington Post.
Maness and Schlichter have active government email addresses ending in ".civ" - meaning they are civilian employees - and are assigned to the Defense Department's undersecretary for personnel and readiness, sources told the Post.
Yet neither influencer has disclosed that they are working for, or did work for, the Pentagon, the Post reported. Even while they were advocating for Hegseth to fire critics at the department, backing Trump's military actions in Venezuela and defending the Defense Secretary's spending on a luxury dinner.
Read on...
Trump threatens to hit Iran 'hard'
Donald Trump has threatened to "hit them hard" after the US and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month, warning that "there will be a response" following Iranian missile strikes on US military bases in Jordan.
He called Iran "officially a failed nation without an airforce, a navy or a currency".
The latest escalation began when US forces struck two Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran was preparing to deploy naval mines in the crucial waterway.
Iran retaliated by targeting US bases, while the UAE said it intercepted an Iranian drone.
The renewed fighting comes as Washington intensifies sanctions aimed at crippling Iran's economy and seeks to loosen Tehran's control over the Strait of Hormuz.
new_text:
Donald Trump's top White House aides are urgently pushing to prevent the Iran war from escalating, after the US ramped up the intensity of its attacks on Wednesday.
The aides want to prevent the war escalating before November's midterm elections to hinder Republican electoral losses, four sources told the Reuters news agency.
Officials will consider once again ramping up military action after the vote in November, but a return to the full-scale conflict is not a fiven, they said.
"We are keeping the pressure on Iran," one White House official said. "But November is a priority."
It comes after Iran vowed to respond with "crushing and devastating blows" after US strikes killed five people attending a wedding party in Iran.
Iranian state media reported explosions across southern coastal areas, including Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island. Tehran also said US strikes hit civilian sites in Hormozgan province and a civilian airport in Kerman province.
One of the strikes hit a home in Kuhestak where a wedding ceremony was taking place, killing five people, including a child, and wounding at least 68 others, according to Hormozgan provincial officials.
Centcom said it concluded its latest barrage against Iranian military targets on Tuesday night.
Pictured: Centcom shares footage of Iranian military target before strike
Trump's aides push to prevent Iran war from escalating - Reuters
Senior aides to Donald Trump are pushing to prevent the Iran war from escalating, after the US ramped up the intensity of its attacks on Wednesday.
The aides want to prevent the war escalating before November's midterm elections to hinder Republican electoral losses, four sources told the Reuters news agency.
Officials will consider once again ramping up military action after the vote in November, but a return to the full-scale conflict is not a fiven, they said.
They said that for now, the administration is focused on tightening the economic pressure on Iran in an effort to extract concessions in any future negotiation that months of military action failed to secure.
"We are keeping the pressure on Iran," one White House official said. "But November is a priority."
Keeping the war mostly contained until then would help prevent the unpopular conflict from dominating the news as Trump's Republicans campaign to defend thin majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives, said the sources, three of whom are White House officials.
Exhausted and demoralised? How US sailors are really coping after six months at sea
While President Trump and his self-styled secretary of state for "War", Pete Hegseth, dismissed it as 'fake news', by all accounts, life for the 5,000 men and women on board the USS Abraham Lincoln had become a living nightmare after more than 260 days at sea without respite.
The nuclear-powered warship left San Diego in November and has, until recently, been stationed in the Middle East to support the U.S. war against Iran. While the Lincoln left the Middle East on August 22 on its way home, with a planned Thailand stop, she has spent a record amount of time at sea without a port visit. Stories abound about poor food, bad hygiene, blocked toilets, intermittent showers, plummeting morale and shredded mental health. Reports in the Military Times and the Stars and Stripes claimed that sailors even tried to jump overboard as the deployment kept going.
Chris Terrill reports:
Oil tankers hit sea mines while transiting Strait of Hormuz, says Tehran
Two oil tankers hit sea mines and were disabled while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday.
In a statement shared by state media, the guards said the tankers had been forced to disembark their crews and were placed in the hands of US operatives to pass through what it called an "illegal route" in the strategic waterway.
It came despite earlier warnings from the Guards' navy about the dangers of crossing the mined passage, the statement added.
Two killed in security incident in Strait of Hormuz, says Saudi shipping company
Two Filipino seafarers have been killed in a security incident in the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's national shipping company, Bahri, said on Wednesday.
The incident involved the company's vessel "SIDR" while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz on August 31, it said.
Bahri did not provide further details - we'll bring you more on this incident as we get it.
Watch: US airstrike hits home where wedding celebration was taking place, Iran says
Pakistan confident US and Iran will 'return to the table'
Pakistan is working with the US and Iran to end their conflict and believes they will soon "return to the table for dialogue".
Foreign ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi made the comments at a regular media briefing on Wednesday.
The visit last month of Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir to Tehran created "considerable momentum" on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, he said.
Moscow helping Iran produce supersonic cruise missiles - report
Iran is secretly developing advanced supersonic cruise missiles with the help of Russia, according to a report.
The C430L programme, which has spanned several years since 2023, has seen Moscow's top missile specialists helping produce the weapons that would significantly strengthen Tehran's military, with the prospect of total peace with the US currently looking bleak.
It was reported by the Financial Times, which dubbed the programme as one of the most "significant known transfers of strategic military technology from Moscow to Tehran".
Moscow is assisting Tehran in developing a ramjet propulsion system, which would enable cruise missiles to fly much faster than the speed of sound, according to military patents and leaked Russian correspondence, the FT reported.
Iranian missile expert Fabian Hinz, an analyst at Conflict Armament Research, told the outlet: "This is the transfer of a highly strategically sensitive military technology from Russia that the Iranians have wanted to acquire for decades.
"A programme like this would require political clearance from the very top in Russia."
Trump insists US has 'almost total control' of Hormuz - recap
Donald Trump has insisted that the US has "almost total control" of the Strait of Hormuz.
"I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing", the US president said of Iran on Truth Social earlier Wednesday morning. "They are just playing out the inevitable. When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?"
Kuwait races to contain fire at a residential complex in capital after drone strike
Firefighters in Kuwait rushed to contain a blaze at a residential complex in the capital after it was struck by an Iranian drone.
Public Fire Force spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammed Al-Gharib said on Wednesday, that the fire had been doused and blamed "a hostile drone" from Iran for the attack.
